name: graph-first-navigation
body:
The codebase-navigator's "graph first" rule is an explicit procedural ordering that applies to ANY question about code or structure — including discovery and enumeration ("what is in this file?", "what does this unit depend on?", "what are the frontends?") — not only to relationship claims (callers/callees/uses/containment). For every such question the FIRST tool call must be a graph query; `read`/`grep`/`glob` are confirmatory — they open the `path` a graph result returned, at its `start_line`/`end_line` — or they read artifacts the graph does not model. The rule must name both artifact classes.

Baseline (actual branch state): the ordering and the artifact-class boundary ALREADY exist — this change-set AMENDS an installed rule, it does not install a new one. `opencode-suite/agents/codebase-navigator.md` rule 1 ("Graph first, then file read") already states the ordering for ANY code/structure question, discovery and enumeration included, and already names both classes (the "In the graph:" / "Not in the graph:" lists). `AGENTS.md` already carries the same qualifier in its "Other tools" section and on the "Read those files with read, grep, or bash" line; `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md` rule 5 already requires every generated agent to inherit the ordering; and the coherence test `rust.apg.tests.e2e.graph_first_rule_stated_in_navigator_prompt_and_guide` (`src/main.rs:5053-5116`) already asserts all of it. (The previous "Observed today (at 0.16.1)" paragraph was stale and self-contradictory: it cited rule numbers 2 and 7 that do not exist and claimed neither a discovery ordering nor an artifact-class boundary was stated, contradicting the installed prompt and the sibling note `requirements.note.graph-first-artifact-class-shrink`.)

0.17.0's genuine delta is ONLY to SHRINK the not-in-graph list. Because the bundled structural scanner graphs every tracked text/config/packaging file, the boundary becomes:
- In the graph: all scanned source (`src/**`), scanned Markdown (`AGENTS.md`/`README.md`, `opencode-suite/**`), and every tracked text/config/packaging file the structural scanner claims — `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` (toml), `install.sh` (sh), `.github/workflows/release.yml` (yaml), `apg/config.json` and `opencode-suite/package.json` (json), `LICENSE` (misc).
- Not in the graph: artifacts no scanner claims even after 0.17.0 — Ruby sources (`Formula/*.rb`, pending `apg-ruby`), binaries, and any path the config scope (`apg/config.json`) excludes.

Acceptance criteria:
- The installed navigator prompt's rule 1 is AMENDED so its "Not in the graph:" list shrinks to Ruby sources (pending `apg-ruby`), binaries and config-excluded paths, and its "In the graph:" list names the tracked text/config/packaging files the structural scanner claims. (The ordering and the dual-class shape are already present and must not regress.)
- `AGENTS.md` carries the corresponding shrunk not-in-graph list; the graph-first qualifier it already carries is unchanged.
- `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md` rule 5 continues to require every generated agent to inherit the graph-first ordering (already present; the amendment must not regress it).
- The existing coherence test `rust.apg.tests.e2e.graph_first_rule_stated_in_navigator_prompt_and_guide` (`src/main.rs:5053-5116`) still passes; if the shrunk list is pinned by assertion, the assertions are added to that same test.
- The observable goal is behavioural: an agent answering a discovery question queries the graph before reaching for a file tool, and knows the tracked text/config/packaging files are now in the graph.
